feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
entry.summary: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.

entry.title: The Fed raises interest rates. And, EU proposes Canada become an 'associate member'
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time in years. And, the European Union has proposed that Canada become its first-ever "associate member."

entry.title: Pressure on global chokepoints drives Asia's increased use of Arctic Trade Routes
entry.summary: Asian nations began pilot voyages over a decade ago to find routes to Europe and the Middle East that were faster and less vulnerable to chokepoints. The ongoing war has added impetus to those efforts.

entry.title: Why reshaping memories may hold the key to raising self-esteem
entry.summary: In a new book, psychologist Marisa Franco explains why it's good to feel good about yourself — and shares a helpful memory technique that we've turned into a printable worksheet.

entry.title: D.C. airspace is complicated. Experts say Trump's arch would add one more risk
entry.summary: The Trump administration wants to build its 250-foot arch near one of the country's busiest runways. The FAA will determine whether that poses a hazard. But independent experts already have concerns.

entry.title: A Sikh truck driver is stabbed amid a rise in anti-South Asian rhetoric
entry.summary: The driver said he was shaken by a violent encounter at a rest stop, which he described as unprovoked.

entry.title: Pediatricians raise the alarm on the effect of Trump's immigration crackdown on kids
entry.summary: The Trump administration has been pursuing a quiet immigration crackdown strategy: limiting access to health care and public services. The American Academy of Pediatrics is sounding the alarm about the impact on children.

entry.title: People's houses are collapsing into the ocean. FEMA gives them no other option
entry.summary: Waterfront homes are collapsing along the coast. Homeowners generally have plenty of warning before their house buckles. So why aren't most houses removed, or at least emptied, before they fall?

entry.title: Big questions - and key logistical details - loom ahead of China-U.S. summit
entry.summary: Despite the lingering questions, China remains optimistic about the summit.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: The Fed raises interest rates for the first time in three years, protests over rising gas prices are being held around the world, Canada's prime minister speaks to European Parliament.
